source.question: Is F-12's missing downhole pressure after October 2010 a reservoir problem or a sensor problem?

submission.summary: F-12's missing downhole pressure after 12 October 2010 is a sensor failure, not a reservoir pressure collapse. The BHP gauge went to zero and stayed there while the well kept flowing for 1 830 days and produced about 1.13 million Sm3 of oil, with normal wellhead pressure and field voidage replacement near 1.

findings.claim: BHP went to zero on 2010-10-12 and stayed missing until end of data, while the well kept flowing: 2 095 days of zero readings include 1 830 flowing days producing about 1.13 million Sm3.
findings.detail: Gauge failure detected around 2010-10-12 (last good BHP 253.9 bar on 2010-10-11). Production issues log zero_gauge_reading set_missing from 2010-10-12 onward for bhp_bar, bht_c and dp_tubing. Well continued at ~1 500 Sm3/d per producing day through Nov-Dec 2010.

findings.claim: Production did not collapse when BHP went missing: F-12 delivered 44 468 Sm3 in November 2010 and 45 218 Sm3 in December 2010 at 96-100% uptime with WHP about 51-52 bar.
findings.detail: Monthly E3: 2010-11 oil 44 468 Sm3, 30 producing days, uptime 0.9588, WHP 50.67 bar, choke 52.94%, bhp null; 2010-12 oil 45 218 Sm3, 31 producing days, uptime 0.9964, WHP 52.46 bar, bhp null. Daily E7 shows 1 400-1 800 Sm3/d and WHP 48-54 bar through Oct-Dec 2010.

findings.claim: Reservoir pressure was supported by waterflood: field replacement ratio was about 1.08 in 2010 and stayed near 1.0 thereafter, so a sudden downhole pressure loss is not expected.
findings.detail: Waterflood field_voidage: 2010 replacement_ratio 1.08 (injection 4 569 394 Sm3 vs oil 1 689 903 Sm3 + water 1 887 595 Sm3), 2011 1.02, 2012 1.02 at reservoir conditions (Bo 1.385). F-12 later produced 4.58 million Sm3 total, sharing 46% of field oil.

result.summary: 30-day median water_cut first goes above 0.05 on 2009-10-31, 21 months after first oil.
30-day median water_cut first goes above 0.5 on 2010-06-04, 28 months after first oil.
Shut in for 12 days from 2010-08-16. Oil rate 1,821 -> 2,000 Sm3/d (+10%) after restart. Same time as F-14.

bhp_bar reads 0 on 2095 days from 2010-10-12 to 2016-09-17 while the well kept flowing on 1830 days (1,133,053 Sm3 oil): a sensor failure, not a pressure collapse. Last good reading: 253.9 on 2010-10-11.

30-day median water_cut first goes above 0.8 on 2012-02-14, 48 months after first oil.
Shut in for 46 days from 2012-08-14. Oil rate 691 -> 728 Sm3/d (+5%) after restart. Same time as F-14.
Shut in for 13 days from 2013-03-12. Oil rate 531 -> 572 Sm3/d (+8%) after restart.

arguments.sql: SELECT date, well, field, issue, raw_value, action FROM production_issues WHERE well='F-12' ORDER BY date

issues.text: water cut above 0.80 (now 0.85); the platform was designed for 0.80
oil rate stepped down 60%, weekly mean 1,259 -> 509 Sm3/d
31 days shut in over the last 180

result.levels: alarm: act now; caution: watch; note: for the record

result.no_trend: WOR is not rising with cumulative oil on 2013-05 to 2016-08: no limit can be projected
result.notes: WOR = water/oil by month; the trend is log10(WOR) against cumulative oil, fitted on up to 36 recent months with WOR >= 1. field_voidage: replacement_ratio is injection over voidage at reservoir conditions (Bo 1.385 m3/Sm3 from PUD p.20, low/high with Bo 1.5/1.27; Bw 1; above the bubble point, so no free gas); surface_ratio is the same in surface volumes, which overstates replacement.

arguments.sql: SELECT date, oil_sm3, water_sm3, bhp_bar, whp_bar, choke_pct, on_stream_hrs FROM production_daily WHERE well='F-12' AND date BETWEEN '2010-10-01' AND '2010-12-31' ORDER BY date
